name: Citizenship by Marriage to an Algerian Citizen

requirements.blocker_text: Code de la Nationalite Algerienne, Article 9: the marriage must be legal and effectively established for at least 3 years, with at least 2 years of continuous, regular residence in Algeria, good conduct and moral character, and sufficient means of subsistence. A separate Wikipedia summary of the code describes the acquisition provision's language as covering marriage 'avec un Algerien ou avec une Algerienne' (to an Algerian man or an Algerian woman), suggesting the acquisition mechanism itself is gender-neutral -- though this was not independently cross-confirmed against the code's full original text in this build, and a separate renunciation-specific clause is worded around an Algerian woman marrying a foreigner rather than the reverse.
requirements.fix_path: Marry an Algerian citizen, maintain the marriage for at least 3 years with at least 2 years of continuous residence in Algeria, and apply.

evidence_required.document: Proof of sufficient means of subsistence

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 2 years continuous residence, within a marriage of at least 3 years

sources.title: Avocat Algerien (Algerian law firm) -- Code de la Nationalite Article 9 (marriage-based acquisition) and Article 10 (naturalization)
Wikipedia (French) -- describes the marriage-acquisition provision's gender-neutral phrasing and a separate renunciation clause specific to Algerian women marrying foreigners

STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to a law firm (tier 3) for the core requirement and Wikipedia (tier 4) for the gender-language detail; a Journal Officiel or other government-hosted primary text was not successfully fetched in this build. HONEST, UNRESOLVED DISCLOSURE: the two sources reviewed do not fully agree on the gender-symmetry question -- the law-firm source describes the requirement in generic terms without specifying gender, while the Wikipedia summary reports the acquisition mechanism's own text names both directions ('avec un Algerien ou avec une Algerienne') but ALSO flags a separate provision specifically addressing an Algerian woman's own nationality upon marrying a foreigner. This build could not fully resolve whether a foreign husband of an Algerian wife has an equivalent, symmetric path to a foreign wife of an Algerian husband -- disclosed as an open question rather than assumed either way, consistent with this dataset's treatment of similar ambiguous cases (e.g. Guatemala's older descent framing). dual_citizenship_allowed left null: neither source addressed whether this route requires renouncing a prior nationality.
